text: BRD Program v4, BRD Epic 1 v4 and BRD Epic 2 v2 are taken as the approved business baseline for this PRD even though none of them carries a status field or an approval record, so the PRD is issued as Draft with an empty approval table and the requirements approval gate stays open.
why: None of the three BRD document control tables has a status or an approval row (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-13), and this run does not stop for a missing approval.
read: Business Requirements Program v4, Epic 1 v4 and Epic 2 v2, all dated 15 November 2026, are the baseline; the PRD approval is pending.
applied_in: Section 1 document control, section 13 approval table
confirm: Product Owner and FDA at the requirements approval gate
impact: The PRD is a Draft baseline; no story is blocked because the story set already exists.

text: The product baseline of this PRD is BRD Program v4 section 5.5 and section 6, BRD Epic 1 v4 section 3.5, BRD Epic 2 v2 section 3.5, FSD P5 Document hub v3 as the latest FSD of the family, TSD P5 Document hub v2 for the data dictionary and the operation list, Architecture v5, the Ownership Map and the Non Functional Specification v3.
why: No earlier PRD exists in the family and the source set names more than one version of the technical and functional specifications; the highest version of each family is the one this run reads.
read: FSD P5 v3 dated 15 November 2026 is the source of the functional detail; Arch v5 wins over it where they disagree (R-PREC rule 1).
impact: A later FSD or TSD version re-baselines the FR and NFR tables.

text: Document generation is in scope of this PRD: letters and notices in wave 1 through the P5 part of notice generation, and contracts, credit applications and mortgage documents in wave 2 under REQ-DCM-012, sourced from the BRD Epic 2 stories, the two TSD operations and the confirmed v5 operation POST /documents/generate.
why: REQ-DCM-012 is a Must requirement and the FSD has no section for it (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-1); the behaviour is confirmed by Architecture v5 slide 16 and by two P5 operations in the Ownership Map.
read: Generation is a product behaviour of rwb-document that consumes the Legal-approved template version held by rwb-comms; this service stores and versions the result.
applied_in: Section 2.2, section 5 CAP-P5-015, section 6 FR-P5-026, section 10.2 and 10.3, section 11 AC-P5-019
impact: A generation FSD section would replace the BRD-derived statement and confirm the wave.

text: Legal hold is a product behaviour of this service, driven by the hold that rwb-case records, and it is released in wave 4 with RWB-AD-021 even though REQ-DCM-016 is an Epic 1 Must; the retention class and the virus scan that the hold overlays are released in wave 1.
why: The hold API belongs to P3 and the only legacy story covering hold and retention administration is an Epic 8 story at release 30 June 2027 (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-2), while the BRD places the requirement in Epic 1.
read: P3 owns the hold decision; P5 owns the effect on expiry and deletion, and the class and the scan land first so that nothing is stored without them.
applied_in: Section 2.3, section 5 CAP-P5-014, section 6 FR-P5-025, section 10.2 and 10.4, section 11 AC-P5-018
impact: If the hold must be released in wave 1, a P5 story and a wave-1 test are added; if P5 must own the hold, the P3 operation moves.

text: E-discovery production and court-ready evidence are in scope of this PRD and are released in wave 2, with the discovery response target left open until Legal counsel sets one.
why: REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018 are Must requirements of Epic 2 with no feature, criterion or operation (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-3) and NFR-073 is open.
read: The production is answered from this service's own metadata, versions and read log; the response target is an open question, never an invented value.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P5-018, section 6 FR-P5-028 and FR-P5-029, section 7 NFR-P5-019, section 10.3, section 11 AC-P5-021
impact: A response target and a discovery operation are needed before wave 2 acceptance.

text: Storage sizing and costing, backup and tested restore, and the records management position are wave 1 obligations of this service, held by the IT lead and the document hub owner together, and the restore evidence is a release gate at every release.
why: REQ-DCM-014, REQ-DCM-015 and REQ-DCM-020 are Must requirements of Epic 1 with no feature, criterion or artifact (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-4), and NFR-071 is open under DL27.
read: The obligations are met by a platform backup service under the bank schedule; this service reports the estate and supplies the restore evidence.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P5-019, section 6 FR-P5-030 and FR-P5-031, section 9, section 10.2, section 11 AC-P5-022 and AC-P5-023
confirm: IT lead with Compliance and Legal
impact: The schedule and the restore evidence are fixed by DL27; the wave does not change.

text: The retention classes named in the FSD acceptance criteria (GENERAL05Y, LEGAL10Y, DOCTYPE-2026.11 and RET-2026.11) are read as examples taken from a reference-table version, not as approved periods; the period behind each class stays open and the retention rule table is read as the versioned table that carries it.
why: NFR-028 states that the periods are not set and DL26 is open (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-5), and the retention rule table has no field list in the TSD or the data dictionary.
read: A document carries the class of its type version in force; the period comes from the retention table; a class without a row is an exception, never a deletion.
applied_in: Section 7 NFR-P5-012, section 8.1, section 6 FR-P5-022, section 10.5
impact: The retention run cannot be accepted until the periods and the retention rule fields are approved.

text: The 26 extracted fields are read as the union of the per-type field definitions delivered in the signed reference load; this PRD requires the count to reconcile with 26 and the two named types to keep their four fields each, and does not enumerate the remaining four types.
why: Only two of the six types name their fields in any source (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-6) and DL19 is open.
read: The extraction build and its evaluation wait on the signed load; no field list is invented here.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P5-011 and FR-P5-016, section 12 OQ-P5-01 and OQ-P5-14
confirm: Business lead with Legal counsel and the Head of NPA
impact: A late field list moves the extraction build and the evaluation pass marks.

text: OCR, document classification and field extraction are reached through a contract owned outside this service, either as an AgentRunCompleted event or as a Temporal child run on queue rwb-document, and malware scanning is a platform security service; P5 owns the intake, the text, the confidence, the review queue, the index and the decision record that carries the versions.
why: No source names the provider, the owner, the contract or the version scheme of the three engines (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-7), while Architecture v5 slide 16 confirms a child agent run and the decision record must carry the versions.
read: The pipeline behaviour is P5's; the engines are external and replaceable; the version of each engine is recorded with the action.
applied_in: Section 2.3, section 7 NFR-P5-017, section 9, section 12 OQ-P5-06
confirm: Solution architect with the AI product owner
impact: A named provider with a different contract changes the integration row and the FR statements that name the OCR, classifier and extractor versions.

text: File intake from branch scanner folders, partner SFTP subfolders and recovery mailboxes is performed by rwb-integration, which hands each file to this service as an intake item; this service records the source, the channel, the capture time, the hash and the duplicate rule and reads no file-system path of its own.
why: The FSD puts the file channels inside P5 while Architecture v5 slide 16 gives P5 no file interface and DP-16 gives file exchange to rwb-integration (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-8).
read: Architecture v5 wins under R-PREC rule 1; the intake contract between P2 and P5 is the boundary.
applied_in: Section 2.3, section 5.1, section 6 FR-P5-020, section 9, section 12 OQ-P5-07
impact: If P5 must poll a channel, a file interface and its infrastructure are added to this service.

text: This service is the system of record: the file is held in Blob with WORM and the metadata, text, fields, custody, signatures and retention are held in `rwb_document`; the ACE Attachment extension declared in the TSD is read as the legacy position and no ACE table holds the authoritative copy.
why: The TSD extends the ACE Attachment object (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-9) while REQ-DCM-002, DT06 and Architecture v5 slides 16 and 21 make the hub the record and forbid a grant on ACE tables (ADR-010, DP-01).
read: Precedence R-PREC rule 1 and ADR-010 both support the hub as the record; the TSD wording is the loser.
applied_in: Section 2.3, section 5.1, section 6 FR-P5-004, section 8.1, section 12 OQ-P5-12
impact: A contrary ruling would add an ACE dependency and break the boundary rule.

text: A signature request is recorded by this service as a document event and a metadata row on the document it belongs to, while the signing journey and the returned signed copy belong to rwb-comms and rwb-treatment; the signature requirement text and its acceptance criteria are not yet written.
why: Architecture v5 and the Ownership Map give P5 the signature table but no requirement, feature or criterion exists (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-10), and RWB-E2-018 is split across three services.
read: P5 records the signature request and the signed version; P5 does not run the signing journey.
applied_in: Section 2.3, section 5.1, section 8.1 signature_request, section 10.5, section 12 OQ-P5-13
confirm: Solution architect with P6 and S2
impact: Signature behaviour may need a requirement of its own and a wave-2 story.

text: JOB-12 is an event-started DocumentIntakeWorkflow with KEDA workers on queue rwb-document, the 15-minute cadence is kept as a schedule that raises the intake, and JOB-17 is a Temporal Schedule in rwb-document on the 1st Sunday of the month.
why: The FSD gives intake as a 15-minute scheduled job (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-11) while Architecture v5 slides 16 and 44 and the Ownership Map replacement give an event-started workflow and a Temporal Schedule.
read: Architecture v5 wins; no Quartz or shared scheduler table is used (ADR-016, DP-10).
impact: The run book, the alerts and the throughput test follow the workflow, not a job entry.

text: Every read of a document and of its extracted fields through this service is logged; the data lake clause of NFR-042 is not carried because no lake copy of the document store exists in the target.
why: NFR-042 still names the data lake copy (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-12) while Architecture v5 removes the lake and DP-17 removes the lake path.
read: The access log covers the document store, the intake items and the free-text search; the lake is out of scope.
impact: None on the build; NFR-042 needs the same correction in its next version.

text: FSD A2.10 and A2.11 are read as one behaviour: the review queue that holds low-confidence intake items and the correction screen that clears them, with the correction recorded in the decision record and fed to the labelled sample; the duplicated criteria are met once.
why: The two features assert the same criteria word for word and neither states the correction feed that RWB-E1-054 requires (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-14).
read: One capability, CAP-P5-010, with two functional requirements; the feed is stated in FR-P5-018.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P5-010, section 6 FR-P5-017 and FR-P5-018, section 11 AC-P5-012
impact: The test set counts one behaviour, not two, which reduces the review test set by the duplicated criteria.

text: The customer on a document is identified by the ACE person key held as `person_key` of type varchar(255), with no foreign key and no reference to an ACE table; the TSD party_id of type uuid is read as the superseded position.
why: The FSD v3 change note replaces party_id with person_key while the TSD still carries party_id (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P5-15), and a foreign key into ACE is forbidden by DP-01 and ADR-014.
read: The FSD change is the later intent and the only reading consistent with the boundary rule; the value is read through the rwb-source-data contract.
applied_in: Section 8.1, section 8.4, section 6 FR-P5-001, section 12 OQ-P5-14
impact: A contrary ruling changes the column, its type and the migration.
